name: Joko Widodo
_note: M2 benchmark expansion: President of Indonesia, 20 Oct 2014 to 20 Oct 2024 (two terms). International benchmark (reference head of government), not part of the ranked Malaysian class. C1 (coalition pivotality) and C2 (governance index) are jurisdiction-specific structural dimensions and are left unrecorded for this reference point rather than imputed without the chamber's seat math; the benchmark anchors the conduct (Layer B) and integrity (A5) scales. Layer B (Editorial Panel) is a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

metrics.justification: No personal criminal charge or conviction of record, to the source date. A 2024 anti-corruption-watchdog listing naming him over the weakening of the anti-graft commission was a reputational finding, not a filed charge (he called it baseless); 2025 anti-corruption questioning of former ministers and projects targeted subordinates, not him personally. Recorded as the subject's own factual status only.

citation.title: Indonesia's Widodo slams 'baseless' report listing him as leading corruption enabler

metrics.justification: COVID-19 handling was mixed: he admitted on 13 Mar 2020 that the government had withheld case information "so as not to stir panic," and Indonesia resisted a national lockdown, but a free mass-vaccination programme (from 13 Jan 2021) reached roughly 175 million fully vaccinated by 2023; he also cut ballooning fuel subsidies in Sep 2022 with offsetting cash transfers. Opaque start, measurable recovery (anchor 2).

citation.title: 'We don't want people to panic': Jokowi says on lack of transparency about COVID cases

metrics.justification: Delivered near-universal health coverage: the JKN/BPJS single-payer scheme reached about 98% of the population (~277 million) by 2024, the world's largest. Against this, the Omnibus Job Creation Law was ruled "conditionally unconstitutional" (Nov 2021) and re-enacted by contested emergency regulation, and the Nusantara new-capital project ran short of committed private funding. One flagship reform delivered, others materially diluted (anchor 3).

citation.title: National Health Insurance JKN Coverage Reaches 98.19 Pct

metrics.justification: Documented institutional erosion: his administration and parliament curbed the anti-corruption commission via the 2019 KPK Law (supervisory board, reduced powers) despite the largest student protests since 1998; and the Constitutional Court ruling (16 Oct 2023) that enabled his son's vice-presidential candidacy led the court's ethics council to find Chief Justice Anwar Usman (his brother-in-law) guilty of a serious ethics violation (7 Nov 2023). Both strongest events are erosion, with no offsetting strengthening located (anchor 1).

citation.title: Ethics Council Removes Anwar Usman from Chief Justice Position

metrics.justification: He admitted on the record (13 Mar 2020) that the government had withheld COVID case details to avoid panic, then shifted to "stay home" messaging; on election neutrality his stated position shifted publicly through 2023-2024 (from "meddling is a moral obligation" to "the president can take sides") without a reconciling explanation. Reversals stated openly but not cleanly explained (anchor 2).

citation.title: 'We don't want people to panic': Jokowi says on lack of transparency about COVID cases
